text:
emily: hey team, day 2 and stuck. i can ssh to hosts over VPN but `docker pull registry.internal.redwood.dev/team/image:latest` fails with TLS handshake timeout. `curl -v https://registry.internal.redwood.dev/v2/` also hangs. windows coworkers hit it fine, i'm on Ubuntu 22.04 desktop with AnyConnect (split-tunnel). anyone seen TLS work for some clients but not others?
rafael: welcome! two quick checks: 1) can you `ping` the registry IP? 2) try `curl --resolve registry.internal.redwood.dev:443:10.40.8.12 -v https://registry.internal.redwood.dev/v2/` to force the host->IP mapping and see if TLS completes.
emily: ping works (ICMP ok). the `curl --resolve` attempt just stalls at "TLS handshake" and then times out. traceroute shows an extra hop through a 10.10.x.x device (looks like a NAT/inspection appliance).\jen: fwiw we've seen middleboxes drop large TLS records when MTU is mismatched over split-tunnel VPNs. quick test: `openssl s_client -connect 10.40.8.12:443 -servername registry.internal.redwood.dev` — does it negotiate? also try lowering MTU on the vpn interface temporarily: `sudo ip link set dev <vpn-iface> mtu 1400` to see if that helps.
emily: `openssl s_client` also hangs. i don't see a tun interface on my laptop (AnyConnect on Linux uses tun0 sometimes). what interface should i target?
rafael: identify the adapter with `ip route get 10.40.8.12` and `ip link`. if the route goes via `eth0` to the windows host equivalent, set MTU there. this is often easiest to test by lowering the MTU on your main NIC (or on docker0) to see if broken paths improve.
emily: lowered MTU to 1400 on my eth0 and `curl` returns the registry json. docker pull still fails though — docker daemon seems to use its own networking (daemon is using systemd-resolved stub?).
jen: docker can hit the host DNS/route differences. try configuring Docker daemon to use the same DNS and set `--mtu` in `/etc/docker/daemon.json`:
```
{
  "mtu": 1400,
  "dns": ["10.40.1.2"]
}
```
then `sudo systemctl restart docker` and retry.
emily: that fixed it, docker pull now streams. thanks! two follow-ups: 1) is this expected/manageable for new hires? 2) should i open an infra ticket for managed laptops?
rafael: great. answer: it's a known split-tunnel edge case when traffic traverses inspection appliances that can't handle large TLS frames. we have docs but it's not universal. please open an infra ticket and link to this thread; infra can push an MTU/DNS policy for company-managed images or update docs for the onboarding checklist.
\infra-bot: Docs: https://wiki.redwood.internal/vpn/mtu-tls-registry and infra ticket template: https://infra.redwood.internal/tickets/new (choose "VPN split-tunnel: MTU/TLS issues").
emily: will open a ticket and drop notes in #onboarding. thanks @rafael @jen! :thumbsup:
